key_insight: A single diffusion-based model can be trained to perform joint spatial and temporal super-resolution across multiple upscaling factors by making the model scale-adaptive, eliminating the need for separate models for each resolution/cadence.
problem_solved: Existing joint spatiotemporal super-resolution models are typically tied to a single pair of spatial and temporal upscaling factors, preventing easy transfer across different spatial resolutions and frame rates—especially problematic for climate and geoscience datasets with varying scales and cadences.
method: Introduce a scale-adaptive conditioning scheme for diffusion models so one trained model can handle multiple spatial and temporal upscaling factors.
Jointly model spatial and temporal super-resolution within the diffusion denoising process, using scale parameters (and possibly multi-resolution conditioning) to guide reconstructions.
Design training and inference protocols that enable reuse of the same model across different SR ratios, improving generalization and transfer to unseen cadences/resolutions.
impact: Enables flexible, reusable super-resolution models for video and climate data that reduce model proliferation and improve adaptability to varying sensor resolutions and sampling rates—saving training cost and improving deployment robustness.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: single diffusion model receiving low-res video + scale-conditioning and outputting high-res frames at arbitrary spatial/temporal scales.
Before/after montage: low-res input, temporally interpolated frames, spatially super-resolved output, and ground truth for visual comparison.
Performance chart: error (or SSIM/PSNR) across multiple spatial and temporal upscaling factors comparing single-scale baselines vs. the scale-adaptive model.
Schema showing scale-conditioning: icons/annotations for spatial scale, temporal cadence, and how they feed into the diffusion denoiser.
paper_title: A Scale-Adaptive Framework for Joint Spatiotemporal Super-Resolution with Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Max Defez, Filippo Quarenghi, Mathieu Vrac, Stephan Mandt, Tom Beucler
